signals_systems.objective: Define continuous and discrete signals and systems; identify time-domain properties such as amplitude, frequency, and phase.

sampling_theorem.objective: State and apply the Nyquist-Shannon sampling theorem; explain aliasing and choose an appropriate sampling rate.

fourier_series.objective: Decompose periodic signals into sinusoidal components using the Fourier series and interpret the frequency spectrum.

fourier_transform.objective: Compute and interpret the Fourier Transform; relate time-domain and frequency-domain representations.

dft_fft.objective: Compute the Discrete Fourier Transform (DFT) and understand how the Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) algorithm reduces complexity.

filtering_basics.objective: Design and apply low-pass, high-pass, and band-pass filters; characterize filters by cutoff frequency and order.

convolution.objective: Compute discrete convolution and understand its role in FIR filtering and system response.

windowing.objective: Explain spectral leakage and apply windowing functions (Hamming, Hanning, Blackman) to reduce it.

stft_spectrogram.objective: Compute the Short-Time Fourier Transform and interpret spectrograms for non-stationary signals.

noise_snr.objective: Define signal-to-noise ratio (SNR); apply averaging and filtering strategies to improve SNR in noisy signals.

notes: 10-topic Signal Processing domain for the curric-agents pilot study.
